_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: The context usage popup toggles from the usage label and closes on outside click. The screen is 1280x800. "The label" is ".context-usage-label"; "the popup" is ".chat-context-popup". Accessible names: an element's name is its aria-label if it has one; otherwise a button's name is its text with whitespace collapsed and trimmed, leaving out aria-hidden parts, and a dialog's name is the text of the element its aria-labelledby refers to; "named X" means the name is exactly X. Only elements that are not display: none count. Perform the steps in order. 1. Navigate to /c/{{SLUG}}. 2. The label should be visible (allow 30s). Its ".context-usage-label-tokens" must not be empty (non-empty textContent), its accessible name must match /^Context usage: .+ tokens$/ (read it from the aria-label attribute), and it should have aria-expanded="false". 3. Click the label: the popup should be visible and contain "LLM call"; its ".usage-popup-title" text should match /^Current context: .+ tokens$/; the label should have aria-expanded="true". 4. The label's aria-controls attribute must be non-empty, and the element with that id must have role="dialog". 5. The popup's ".token-cost-graph" and ".token-cost-graph-svg" should be visible. 6. Click the label again: the popup should be hidden and the label should have aria-expanded="false". 7. Click the label: the popup should be visible. Click ".messages-container" 10 pixels right and 10 pixels down from its top-left corner: the popup should be hidden and the label should have aria-expanded="false". 8. Click the label: the popup should be visible. Press Escape: the popup should be hidden and the label should have aria-expanded="false".
